query: For high-entropy-alloy materials intended for self-lubricating moving components, what single intervention could reduce both coefficient of friction and wear rate across a wide service-temperature range? Formulate one hypothesis that identifies the intervention, explains its mechanism, predicts the improvement relative to the untreated alloy, defines the conditions under which it should remain effective, cites prior evidence supporting it, and proposes an experiment whose outcome could falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Adding 5 vol% hexagonal boron nitride (h-BN) nanoparticles to a solution-annealed CoCrFeMnNi high-entropy alloy (HEA) will reduce both steady-state coefficient of friction and wear rate by at least 30 % and 50 %, respectively, over the service-temperature range 25–600 °C relative to the untreated HEA, owing to the in situ formation of a self-lubricating h-BN–rich tribofilm that lowers interfacial shear and protects the substrate.
generation.material_initial_state: Solution-annealed, equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi HEA with no solid-lubricant phases
generation.intervention: Incorporation of 5 vol% h-BN nanoparticles, uniformly dispersed by powder-metallurgy blending and hot consolidation
generation.conditions: Dry sliding under 5–20 N normal load, 0.1–1 m/s sliding speed, temperatures from 25 °C up to 600 °C, relative humidity ≤ 30 %
generation.structural_mediator: A lamellar, h-BN–rich tribofilm formed at the sliding interface
generation.mechanism: Under load and sliding, h-BN layers shear easily via weak van der Waals bonding and form a protective film that prevents direct metal–metal contact, thus reducing both friction and material removal
generation.predicted_outcome: Across the 25–600 °C range, coefficient of friction falls by ≥ 30 % and wear rate by ≥ 50 % compared to the untreated HEA
generation.baseline: Tribological performance of the untreated CoCrFeMnNi HEA under identical test conditions
generation.boundary: Lubrication effectiveness is expected to persist up to 600 °C; above ~600 °C, oxidation of h-BN to B₂O₃ may degrade the tribofilm
generation.uncertainty: Stability and integrity of the h-BN tribofilm between 400 °C and 600 °C under humid conditions are not well established

falsification_experiment.design: Perform pin-on-disk tests on both untreated and 5 vol% h-BN–doped HEA specimens at 25 °C, 200 °C, 400 °C and 600 °C under 10 N load and 0.2 m/s sliding speed. Run each condition until steady state is reached.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the h-BN–doped HEA fails to exhibit at least a 20 % reduction in both friction and wear rate relative to the untreated HEA in at least three of the four temperature conditions, the hypothesis is falsified.
